subject: maths
card: What each digit is worth, big numbers up to a million, rounding and decimals.
title: Place value
seo_title: Place value practice: digits, rounding and decimals (KS2, ages 9 to 11)
description: Learn place value step by step with place value charts: the value of each digit, numbers up to 1,000,000, comparing and ordering, rounding, tenths and hundredths, and multiplying and dividing by 10, 100 and 1,000. Free practice for ages 9 to 11.
intro: The same digit can be worth 5 or 5,000, depending on where it sits. Learn how place value works and big numbers, rounding and decimals all start to make sense.

units.title: What is each digit worth?
units.blurb: Ones, tens, hundreds and thousands in a place value chart.

learn.p: Each place in a number has a value. From the right: **ones (O)**, **tens (T)**, **hundreds (H)**, **thousands (Th)**. Each column is worth 10 times the column on its right.
In 3,528 the 5 is in the hundreds column, so it is worth **500**. The 3 is worth 3,000, the 2 is worth 20 and the 8 is worth 8. Together: 3,000 + 500 + 20 + 8 = 3,528.
In 4,072 there are no hundreds, so we write a 0 to hold the place. Without it, 4,072 would turn into 472, a very different number!

questions.hint: Which column is the 7 in? Count from the right: ones, tens, hundreds…
questions.explain: The 7 is in the hundreds column, so it is worth 700.

questions.q: Which number is shown in the chart?
questions.hint: Read the digits from left to right, and don't skip the 0.
questions.explain: 6 thousands, 0 hundreds, 3 tens and 5 ones make 6,035.

questions.q: What is the value of the 4 in 4,019?
questions.hint: The 4 is in the thousands column.
questions.explain: The 4 is worth 4,000 (four thousand).

questions.hint: Put each part in its own column: thousands, hundreds, tens, ones.
questions.explain: 5 thousands, 3 hundreds, 6 tens and 2 ones make 5,362.

questions.hint: There are no hundreds. What goes in the hundreds column?
questions.explain: 8 thousands, 0 hundreds, 4 tens and 1 one: 8,041.

questions.q: In which number is the 3 worth 30?
questions.hint: Worth 30 means 3 tens. Find the number with a 3 in the tens column.
questions.explain: In 1,234 the 3 is in the tens column, so it is worth 30.

questions.hint: Add 1 to the hundreds digit. 9 hundreds + 1 hundred = 10 hundreds = 1 thousand.
questions.explain: 2,950 + 100 = 3,050. The hundreds go from 9 to 10, so we carry 1 into the thousands.

questions.hint: Take 1 away from the thousands digit.

units.title: Big numbers up to a million
units.blurb: Ten thousands, hundred thousands and one million.

learn.p: After thousands come **ten thousands (TTh)** and **hundred thousands (HTh)**. Then one million: 1,000,000.
We put a comma every three digits from the right. 472,105 is read “four hundred and seventy-two **thousand**, one hundred and five”. The part before the comma tells you how many thousands.
One million is a thousand thousands: 1,000,000. It has six zeros.

questions.hint: Count the columns from the right: O, T, H, Th, TTh…
questions.explain: The 6 is in the ten thousands column, so it is worth 60,000.

questions.q: How do you write “forty-five thousand, two hundred and eight” in digits?
questions.hint: Forty-five thousand is 45,___. Then two hundred and eight goes after the comma, using 3 digits.
questions.explain: 45 thousand, then 208: 45,208.

options: Seven hundred and three thousand and fifty
Seventy thousand, three hundred and fifty
Seven hundred and thirty thousand and five
questions.hint: The part before the comma is how many thousands: 703.
questions.explain: 703 thousand, then 050 = fifty. So 703,050 is seven hundred and three thousand and fifty.

questions.q: How many thousands make one million?
questions.explain: 1,000 × 1,000 = 1,000,000. A million is a thousand thousands.

questions.hint: Add 1 to the ten thousands digit.
questions.explain: 285,600 + 10,000 = 295,600. The ten thousands digit goes from 8 to 9.

questions.hint: Put each part in its column. Which columns are empty?
Count the digits first.
questions.explain: 1,000,000 has 7 digits; the others have 6. It's one more than 999,999.

units.title: Comparing and ordering
units.blurb: Which is bigger? Use the < and > signs.

learn.p: If two whole numbers have a different number of digits, the one with more digits is bigger. 10,000 is bigger than 9,999.
Compare the digits from the **left**. 4,385 and 4,358: thousands are the same (4), hundreds are the same (3), tens: 8 is more than 5. So 4,385 is bigger.
**>** means “is greater than” and **<** means “is less than”. The open mouth faces the bigger number: 4,385 > 4,358.

questions.q: Which sign goes in the gap? 6,214 ___ 6,241
questions.hint: Compare from the left. The thousands and hundreds are the same. Look at the tens.
questions.explain: 1 ten is less than 4 tens, so 6,214 < 6,241.

questions.q: Which sign goes in the gap? 30,500 ___ 9,950
questions.hint: How many digits does each number have?

questions.q: Which list is in order from smallest to biggest?
questions.hint: All the numbers start with 2 thousand. Compare the hundreds next.
questions.explain: Hundreds: 0, 8, 8, 9. The two with 8 hundreds: 2,809 has 0 tens and 2,890 has 9 tens. So the order is 2,089; 2,809; 2,890; 2,908.

questions.hint: It must have 45 thousand and something more.
questions.explain: 45,600 is more than 45,000 and less than 46,000.

questions.q: What is the biggest number you can make with the digits 3, 8, 1 and 6? Use each digit once.
questions.hint: Put the biggest digit in the column worth the most.
questions.explain: Biggest digit in the thousands, then the next: 8,631.

questions.q: What is the smallest 4-digit number you can make with 5, 0, 2 and 7? Use each digit once.
questions.hint: A 4-digit number can't start with 0. Start with the smallest digit that isn't 0.
questions.explain: 2 in the thousands, then 0, 5, 7: 2,057.

questions.hint: Compare the ten thousands digits: 7 and 6.
questions.explain: 7 ten thousands is more than 6 ten thousands, so 70,001 > 69,999.

learn.p: To round 63 to the nearest 10, find the two tens it sits between: 60 and 70. 63 is nearer to 60, so 63 rounds to **60**.
Rounding to the nearest 100? Look at the **tens** digit. To the nearest 1,000? Look at the **hundreds** digit. If it is 0 to 4, round down. If it is 5 to 9, round up.
85 is exactly halfway between 80 and 90. The rule is: halfway rounds **up**, so 85 rounds to 90. And 2,500 rounds to 3,000 to the nearest 1,000.

questions.hint: 47 is between 40 and 50. Which is nearer?
questions.explain: 47 is 3 away from 50 and 7 away from 40, so it rounds to 50.

questions.hint: Look at the tens digit: 3.
questions.explain: The tens digit is 3 (0 to 4), so round down: 400.

questions.hint: Look at the tens digit. Is it 5 or more?
questions.explain: The tens digit is 5, so round up: 1,700.

questions.hint: Look at the hundreds digit: 4.
questions.explain: The hundreds digit is 4, so round down: 6,000.

questions.hint: 35 is exactly halfway between 30 and 40. Remember the rule for halfway.
questions.explain: Halfway rounds up, so 35 rounds to 40.

questions.hint: 297 is between 290 and 300.
questions.explain: 297 is 3 away from 300 and 7 away from 290, so it rounds to 300.

questions.q: A number rounded to the nearest 10 is 80. Which could it be?
questions.hint: Numbers from 75 up to 84 round to 80.
questions.explain: 76 rounds to 80. 74 rounds to 70, 85 and 86 round to 90.

questions.q: A football ground holds 24,763 people. Round this to the nearest 1,000.
questions.hint: Look at the hundreds digit: 7.
questions.explain: The hundreds digit is 7 (5 or more), so round up: 25,000.

units.title: Tenths and hundredths
units.blurb: Decimals in the place value chart.

learn.p: Columns keep going to the right of the decimal point. The first is **tenths (t)**, then **hundredths (h)**. 3.25 means 3 ones, 2 tenths and 5 hundredths.
One tenth is 1 whole cut into 10 equal parts: 0.1 = {1/10}. So 0.7 = {7/10}.
One hundredth is 1 whole cut into 100 equal parts: 0.01 = {1/100}. 0.25 means 25 hundredths, the same as {25/100}. Money uses hundredths: £1.25 is 1 pound and 25 pence.

questions.hint: The first digit after the point is tenths.
questions.explain: The 4 is just after the decimal point, so it is worth 4 tenths (0.4).

questions.hint: 3 tenths goes in the first column after the point.
9 hundredths goes in the second column after the point. What goes in the tenths?
questions.explain: No tenths and 9 hundredths: 0.09.

questions.hint: Compare the tenths digits first.
questions.explain: 0.5 has 5 tenths; 0.45 and 0.405 have 4 tenths; 0.09 has none. So 0.5 is biggest, even though it has fewer digits.

questions.hint: 4 ones, 0 tenths, 6 hundredths.
questions.explain: 4 ones, 0 tenths and 6 hundredths: 4.06.

questions.hint: 1 tenth = 10 hundredths.
questions.explain: 3 tenths = 30 hundredths, because each tenth is 10 hundredths.

questions.q: Round 6.8 to the nearest whole number.
questions.hint: 6.8 is between 6 and 7. Look at the tenths digit.
questions.explain: The tenths digit is 8 (5 or more), so round up: 7.

units.title: × and ÷ by 10, 100 and 1,000
units.blurb: Slide the digits along the columns.

learn.p: Multiplying by 10 moves every digit **one place to the left**, so each digit is worth 10 times more. 34 × 10 = 340. 3.4 × 10 = 34.
Dividing by 10 moves every digit **one place to the right**. 340 ÷ 10 = 34. 34 ÷ 10 = 3.4. 7 ÷ 10 = 0.7.
× 100 moves the digits 2 places, × 1,000 moves them 3 places. ÷ 100 and ÷ 1,000 move them 2 and 3 places to the right. 4.5 × 100 = 450 and 2,600 ÷ 1,000 = 2.6.

questions.hint: Move each digit one place to the left.
Move each digit one place to the right.
× 1,000 moves the digits 3 places to the left.
÷ 100 moves the digits 2 places to the right.
The 2 ones become 2 tens, and the 5 tenths become 5 ones.
9 ones become 9 tenths.
Move each digit two places to the left.

questions.q: A pack of 1,000 sheets of paper costs £6. How many pence is that for each sheet? (£6 = 600p)
questions.hint: Work out 600 ÷ 1,000.
questions.explain: 600 ÷ 1,000 = 0.6, so each sheet costs 0.6p (less than one penny!).
